subject.title: Track OpenClaw seams needed for full imported-plugin parity

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor staged public contracts for these imported-plugin seams, and which seam should establish the first supported trust and compatibility model?
rationale: The requested APIs expose host-owned lifecycle, authorization, authentication, and bundle behavior; choosing their permanent public contracts and sequencing cannot be resolved safely from Babelfish implementation details alone.

options.title: Sponsor staged host contracts
options.body: Approve the architectural direction and split the work into narrow host-owned proposals, beginning with one well-scoped seam and its security model.

options.title: Keep capabilities unsupported
options.body: Retain explicit support-matrix gaps until OpenClaw independently exposes stable generic contracts.

options.title: Permit Babelfish approximations
options.body: Allow local compatibility implementations despite lifecycle and security-semantic differences from the host-owned behavior.

recommendation.title: Sponsor staged host contracts
recommendation.body: Approve the architectural direction and split the work into narrow host-owned proposals, beginning with one well-scoped seam and its security model.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository-member author has already framed the cross-project requirements and is the best available coordinator for obtaining the necessary host decisions.
